exposure: transport method (transport incubator vs. NICU care station)
type of respiratory support (nasal CPAP vs. intratracheal intubation)
outcome: prevalence and duration of ventilator disconnections
cohort: The study included 40 inborn preterm infants undergoing postdelivery room care.
finding: The study found that infants transferred in a transport incubator had shorter postdelivery room care duration, extremely low birth weight infants spent less time in prone position, and infants on nasal CPAP experienced longer ventilator disconnection times, particularly if over 1000g or transported in an incubator.
birth_weight: Extremely low birth weight (ELBW) infants and infants with body weight >1000g were included.
